baselineDisplay.text:
Step 1: Intensive reading.
Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: What would have happened if only two of the sixteen water-tight compartments had been flooded?
Vocabulary:
Southampton n. 南安普敦（英国港口城市）
lookout n. 瞭望员
collision n. 碰撞
colossal adj. 庞大的
narrowly adv. 刚刚，勉强地
watertight adj. 不漏水的
miss v. 避开
compartment n. （轮船的）密封舱
slight adj. 轻微的
tremble v. 震颤
flood v. 充满水
faint adj. 微弱的
float v. 漂浮，飘浮
horror n. 恐惧
tragic adj. 悲惨的
abandon v. 抛弃
liner n. 班船
plunge v. 投入，跳入
voyage n. 航行
lifeboat n. 救生船
iceberg n. 冰山
Passage:
The great ship, Titanic, sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912. She was carrying 1,316 passengers and a crew of 891. Even by modern standards, the 46,000 ton Titanic was a colossal ship. At that time, however, she was not only the largest ship that had ever been built, but was regarded as unsinkable, for she had sixteen watertight compartments. Even if two of these were flooded, she would still be able to float. The tragic sinking of this great liner will always be remembered, for she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life.
巨轮“泰坦尼克”号 1912 年 4 月 10 日从南安普敦起锚驶向纽约。船上载有 1316 名乘客与 891 名船员。即便用现代标准来衡量，46000 吨的“泰坦尼克”号也算得上一艘巨轮了。当时，这艘轮船不仅是造船史上建造的最大的一艘船，而且也被认为是不会沉没的。因为船由 16 个密封舱组成，即使有两个舱进水，仍可漂浮在水面上。然而，这艘巨轮首航就下沉，造成大批人员死亡。人们将永远记着这艘巨轮的沉没惨剧。
Notes:
1 sail for，驶往……。
2 even by modern standards，即使依照现代标准来衡量。by 作“依照”、“按照”讲。
3 regarded as unsinkable，被认为是不会沉没的。regard … as…当“把……当作……”讲。
4 she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life，她首航就下沉，造成大批人员死亡。go down 是“下沉”的意思。
Four days after setting out, while the Titanic was sailing across the icy waters of the North Atlantic, a huge iceberg was suddenly spotted by a lookout. After the alarm had been given, the great ship turned sharply to avoid a direct collision. The Titanic turned just in time, narrowly missing the immense wall of ice which rose over 100 feet out of the water beside her. Suddenly, there was a slight trembling sound from below, and the captain went down to see what had happened. The noise had been so faint that no one thought that the ship had been damaged. Below, the captain realized to his horror that the Titanic was sinking rapidly, for five of her sixteen watertight compartments had already been flooded! The order to abandon ship was given and hundreds of people plunged into the icy water. As there were not enough lifeboats for everybody, 1,500 lives were lost.
“泰坦尼克”起航后的第 4 天，它正行驶在北大西洋冰冷的海面上。突然，瞭望员发现一座冰山。警报响过不久，巨轮急转弯，以避免与冰山正面相撞。“泰坦尼克”这个弯拐得及时，紧贴着高出海面 100 英尺的巨大的冰墙擦过去。突然，从船舱下部传来一声轻微的颤音，船长走下船舱去查看究竟。由于这个声音非常轻，没人会想到船身已遭损坏。在下面，船长惊恐地发现“泰坦尼克”号正在急速下沉，16 个密封舱已有 5 个进水。于是，他发出了弃船的命令，几百人跳进了冰冷刺骨的海水里。由于没有足够的救生艇运载所有乘客，结果 1500 人丧生。
Notes:
5 narrowly missing，勉强避开。
6 Below, the captain realized to his horror，在下面，船长惊恐地发现。 below 是个副词。
10.2【阅读理解】The loss of the Titanic
Step 2: Comprehension questions.
Comprehension:
1 On what date did the Titanic sail for New York from Southampton? (April 10th, 1912.)
2 How many passengers was she carrying and how many crew? (1,316 passengers and a crew of 891.)
3 How many tons was the Titanic? (46,000.)
4 How did she compare with other ships at that time? (She was the largest ship that had ever been built.)
5 Why was she regarded as unsinkable? (Because she had sixteen watertight compartments.)
6 If these were flooded, would the ship still float? (No, she wouldn't.)
7 Had the Titanic ever sailed before? (No, she hadn't.)
8 It was her first voyage, wasn't it? (Yes, it was.)
9 How many days had she been at sea when the iceberg was spotted? (Four days.)
10 Where was the ship at the time? (In the North Atlantic.)
11 What did she do to avoid direct collision? (Turned sharply.)
12 How high was the wall of ice? (100 feet.)
13 What was heard from below? (A slight trembling sound.)
14 What did the captain do? (He went down to see what had happened.)
15 Did the captain think the ship had been damaged? (No, he didn't.)
16 Why did no one think the ship had been damaged? (The noise had been so faint.)
17 What was actually happening to the ship? (She was sinking rapidly.)
18 How many of her compartments had been flooded? (Five.)
19 What order was given to the people on board? (Abandon ship.)
20 Why were so many lives lost? (Because there weren't enough lifeboats.)
10.3【拓展写作】The loss of the Titanic
Step 3: Composition
In not more than 200 words write an imaginary account of what happened on the Titanic immediately after the order to abandon ship was given. Use the ideas given below. Do not write more than three paragraphs.
Title: Abandon ship.
Introduction: Order to abandon ship unexpected — everybody unprepared.
Development: Immediate effect — panic and confusion — people rushing in all directions — crew came up from below — lifeboats lowered — people jumped overboard — struggle to get into lifeboats — lifeboats full
Conclusion: Titanic sank rapidly — people in water — cries of despair — lifeboats moved away.
Key to composition
Abandon ship
The Titanic began to sink, slowly at first. The order to abandon ship was unexpected, so passengers and crew were completely unprepared. It was the middle of the night. Some people were asleep in their cabins. Others were on deck admiring the brilliant night sky and the giant icebergs rising above them. Others were eating and dancing in the wonderful ballrooms on the ship.
The immediate effect was panic and confusion. People began rushing in all directions, wondering what to do next. The cold was indescribable and many passengers were still in their night clothes. Members of the crew came up from below and began to lower the lifeboats. It was a case of women and children first, but it soon became obvious that there weren't enough lifeboats for everyone, so people jumped overboard into the freezing water in order to save their lives. Some of those swimming in the water struggled to get into the lifeboats, but most of them were already full.
The Titanic sank rapidly, carrying many people down with it. There were cries of despair from people in the water as they watched the lifeboats moving away and were left to drown in the icy ocean.
课外练习：
1 When the Titanic set out from Southampton ________.
(a) she was carrying a very large cargo
(b) she was making a voyage which is only attempted by very large ships
(c) only two of her watertight compartments were flooded
(d) she was sailing on her maiden voyage
2 What happened once the iceberg had been spotted?
(a) The Titanic got lost in the icy waters of the North Atlantic.
(b) The alarm was given that there was collision ahead.
(c) The Titanic quickly changed her course.
(d) The Titanic turned just as the iceberg rose steeply out of the water.
3 The Titanic sank because ________.
(a) she had been badly damaged by an iceberg
(b) the captain was slow to realize the true nature of the damage
(c) no more than five of her watertight compartments had been flooded
(d) instead of trying to save her, people plunged into the water
4 ________ were 1,316 passengers and a crew of 891.
(a) On her board
(b) On board her
(c) Boarding he
(d) On boarding her
5 No one thought she ________ sink, for she had sixteen watertight compartments.
(a) would be possible to
(b) would be able to
(c) should
(d) could possibly
6 She ________ four days when huge iceberg was suddenly spotted.
(a) sailed
(b) was sailing
(c) has sailed
(d) had been sailing
7 So faint ________ that no one thought...
(a) the noise was
(b) had been the noise
(c) it was the noise
(d) it had been the noise
8 As there were ________ lifeboats for everybody...
(a) as little
(b) so little
(c) very few
(d) too few
9 The great ship ________ sharply to avoid direct collision.
(a) veered
(b) changed
(c) went back
(d) cornered
10 The Titanic turned ________ narrowly missing the immense wall...
(a) in next to no time
(b) on sudden impulse
(c) with no time to spare
(d) nearly on time
11 The captain went down to ________.
(a) explore
(b) investigate
(c) examine
(d) inquire
12 There was not enough ________ in the lifeboats for everybody.
(a) room
(b) place
(c) volume
(d) area
答案：1 d 2 c 3 a 4 b 5 d 6 d 7 b 8 d 9 a 10 c 11 b 12 a

display.text:
Step 1: Intensive reading.
Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: What would have happened if only two of the sixteen watertight compartments had been flooded?
Vocabulary:
Southampton n. 南安普敦（英国港口城市）
lookout n. 瞭望员
collision n. 碰撞
colossal adj. 庞大的
narrowly adv. 刚刚，勉强地
watertight adj. 不漏水的
miss v. 避开
compartment n. 舱；隔间（watertight compartment 指水密舱）
slight adj. 轻微的
tremble v. 震颤
flood v. 充满水
faint adj. 微弱的
float v. 漂浮，飘浮
horror n. 恐惧
tragic adj. 悲惨的
abandon v. 抛弃
liner n. 定期客轮；班轮
plunge v. 投入，跳入
voyage n. 航行
lifeboat n. 救生艇
iceberg n. 冰山
Passage:
编者说明：本课据1912年英国调查报告及档案馆资料校正叙事。人数采用该报告在离开 Queenstown 后的统计口径；不同历史资料的名单和总数并不完全相同。gross registered tonnage 是登记容积指标，不能当作船舶重量或排水量。
The great ship Titanic sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912. According to the British inquiry, she carried 1,316 passengers and 885 crew after leaving Queenstown. With a gross registered tonnage of about 46,328, she was a colossal ship for her time. She was the largest ship then built and was widely regarded as practically unsinkable, partly because she had sixteen watertight compartments. She was designed to remain afloat with any two compartments flooded. The tragic sinking of this great liner is remembered because she went down on her maiden transatlantic voyage with heavy loss of life.
巨轮“泰坦尼克”号于1912年4月10日从南安普敦启航驶向纽约。根据英国调查报告，离开昆士敦后，船上有1,316名乘客和885名船员。其登记总吨位约为46,328，在当时是一艘庞大的轮船。它是当时建成的最大船舶，并被广泛视为几乎不会沉没，原因之一是它有16个水密舱。设计上，即使任意两个舱进水，它仍能保持漂浮。然而，这艘巨轮在首次跨大西洋航行中沉没，造成重大人员伤亡，成为令人难忘的悲剧。
Notes:
1 sail for，驶往……。
2 by modern standards，按照现代标准。by 在这里表示“依照、按照”；本课历史叙述改用 for her time（就它所处的时代而言），避免把教材成文时的比较当作当代船舶排名。
3 regarded as unsinkable，被认为是不会沉没的。regard … as…当“把……当作……”讲。
4 she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life，她首航就下沉，造成大批人员死亡。go down 是“下沉”的意思。
Four days after leaving Southampton, the Titanic was crossing the North Atlantic when a lookout spotted an iceberg. The warning was given and the ship turned, but her starboard side struck the ice below the waterline. Captain Smith came to the bridge, and the damage was investigated. The British inquiry identified damage in six forward compartments. Flooding of the first five alone was enough to doom the ship, as water could spill over the bulkheads into further compartments. Orders were given to prepare the boats and bring passengers on deck. There was not enough lifeboat capacity for everyone, and some boats left without a full load. The Titanic sank in the early hours of April 15th, about two hours and forty minutes after the collision. About 1,500 people lost their lives.
从南安普敦出发四天后，“泰坦尼克”号正在穿越北大西洋，一名瞭望员发现了冰山。警报发出后，船开始转向，但右舷水线以下仍撞上了冰。史密斯船长来到驾驶台，船员开始检查损伤。英国调查报告列出了前部六个舱的损伤。仅最前面的五个舱进水就足以使船无法维持漂浮，因为水会越过舱壁流入后面的舱室。船上下令准备救生艇，并把乘客带到甲板上。救生艇容量不足以容纳所有人，有些艇还未满载就离开了。4月15日凌晨，碰撞发生约两小时四十分钟后，“泰坦尼克”号沉没，约1,500人丧生。
Notes:
5 narrowly missing，险些碰上但最终避开。泰坦尼克号实际与冰山发生了侧面碰撞，不能把原教材的这一短语误读为完全避开冰山。
6 to one's horror，使某人惊恐的是；below 作副词时可表示“在下面”。
10.2【阅读理解】The loss of the Titanic
Step 2: Comprehension questions.
Comprehension:
1 On what date did the Titanic sail for New York from Southampton? (April 10th, 1912.)
2 According to the British inquiry, how many passengers and crew were aboard after Queenstown? (1,316 passengers and 885 crew.)
3 What was her approximate gross registered tonnage? (46,328.)
4 How did she compare with other ships at that time? (She was the largest ship that had ever been built.)
5 What design feature helped create confidence in her safety? (Her sixteen watertight compartments.)
6 Was she designed to remain afloat if only two compartments flooded? (Yes.)
7 Had she completed a previous transatlantic voyage? (No.)
8 Was this her maiden transatlantic voyage? (Yes.)
9 How many days had she been at sea when the iceberg was spotted? (Four days.)
10 Where was the ship at the time? (In the North Atlantic.)
11 What did the ship do after the warning? (She turned.)
12 When did the Titanic sink? (In the early hours of April 15th, 1912.)
13 Where did the iceberg strike the ship? (On the starboard side below the waterline.)
14 Where did Captain Smith go? (To the bridge.)
15 Did the turn prevent a collision? (No.)
16 Why could flooding spread beyond the first compartments? (Water could spill over the bulkheads.)
17 What happened as the flooding spread? (The ship sank.)

10.3【拓展写作】The loss of the Titanic
Step 3: Composition
In not more than 200 words write an imaginary account of what happened on the Titanic immediately after the order to abandon ship was given. Use the ideas given below. Do not write more than three paragraphs.
Title: Abandon ship.
Introduction: A fictional passenger is told to put on a lifebelt and go on deck.
Development: People wait near the boats — some hesitate to leave — a mother and child enter a boat — the boat is lowered with empty seats.
Conclusion: The ship disappears — survivors wait in the cold — rescue comes later.
Key to composition
Abandon ship
A steward knocked on the cabin door and told Anna to put on her lifebelt. She wrapped a coat around her daughter and led her upstairs. On deck, small groups of passengers stood beside the boats, trying to understand what was happening. Some still believed the great ship was the safest place to remain.
An officer called for women and children. Anna lifted her daughter into a lifeboat and followed. The boat began to descend while several seats were still empty. Looking up, she could see people waiting on the brilliantly lit deck. The distance between them grew as the crew rowed away.
For a long time, Anna watched the ship against the dark sky. Then its lights vanished, and cries carried across the water. She held her daughter close and waited in the bitter cold. When another ship finally appeared, she felt relief mixed with grief for those who would never arrive.

Try to answer the question below while you’re reading:
Question: What would have happened if only two of the sixteen watertight compartments had been flooded?
Vocabulary:

lookout n. 瞭望员
collision n. 碰撞
colossal adj. 庞大的
narrowly adv. 刚刚，勉强地
watertight adj. 不漏水的
miss v. 避开
compartment n. 舱；隔间（watertight compartment 指水密舱）
slight adj. 轻微的

flood v. 充满水
faint adj. 微弱的
float v. 漂浮，飘浮
horror n. 恐惧
tragic adj. 悲惨的
abandon v. 抛弃
liner n. 定期客轮；班轮

voyage n. 航行

Passage:
编者说明：本课据1912年英国调查报告及档案馆资料校正叙事。人数采用该报告在离开 Queenstown 后的统计口径；不同历史资料的名单和总数并不完全相同。gross registered tonnage 是登记容积指标，不能当作船舶重量或排水量。

The great ship Titanic sailed for New York from Southampton on April 10th, 1912. According to the British inquiry, she carried 1,316 passengers and 885 crew after leaving Queenstown. With a gross registered tonnage of about 46,328, she was a colossal ship for her time. She was the largest ship then built and was widely regarded as practically unsinkable, partly because she had sixteen watertight compartments. She was designed to remain afloat with any two compartments flooded. The tragic sinking of this great liner is remembered because she went down on her maiden transatlantic voyage with heavy loss of life.
巨轮“泰坦尼克”号于1912年4月10日从南安普敦启航驶向纽约。根据英国调查报告，离开昆士敦后，船上有1,316名乘客和885名船员。其登记总吨位约为46,328，在当时是一艘庞大的轮船。它是当时建成的最大船舶，并被广泛视为几乎不会沉没，原因之一是它有16个水密舱。设计上，即使任意两个舱进水，它仍能保持漂浮。然而，这艘巨轮在首次跨大西洋航行中沉没，造成重大人员伤亡，成为令人难忘的悲剧。
Notes:
1 sail for，驶往……。
2 by modern standards，按照现代标准。by 在这里表示“依照、按照”；本课历史叙述改用 for her time（就它所处的时代而言），避免把教材成文时的比较当作当代船舶排名。
3 regarded as unsinkable，被认为是不会沉没的。regard … as…当“把……当作……”讲。
4 she went down on her first voyage with heavy loss of life，她首航就下沉，造成大批人员死亡。go down 是“下沉”的意思。

Four days after leaving Southampton, the Titanic was crossing the North Atlantic when a lookout spotted an iceberg. The warning was given and the ship turned, but her starboard side struck the ice below the waterline. Captain Smith came to the bridge, and the damage was investigated. The British inquiry identified damage in six forward compartments. Flooding of the first five alone was enough to doom the ship, as water could spill over the bulkheads into further compartments. Orders were given to prepare the boats and bring passengers on deck. There was not enough lifeboat capacity for everyone, and some boats left without a full load. The Titanic sank in the early hours of April 15th, about two hours and forty minutes after the collision. About 1,500 people lost their lives.

从南安普敦出发四天后，“泰坦尼克”号正在穿越北大西洋，一名瞭望员发现了冰山。警报发出后，船开始转向，但右舷水线以下仍撞上了冰。史密斯船长来到驾驶台，船员开始检查损伤。英国调查报告列出了前部六个舱的损伤。仅最前面的五个舱进水就足以使船无法维持漂浮，因为水会越过舱壁流入后面的舱室。船上下令准备救生艇，并把乘客带到甲板上。救生艇容量不足以容纳所有人，有些艇还未满载就离开了。4月15日凌晨，碰撞发生约两小时四十分钟后，“泰坦尼克”号沉没，约1,500人丧生。
Notes:
5 narrowly missing，险些碰上但最终避开。泰坦尼克号实际与冰山发生了侧面碰撞，不能把原教材的这一短语误读为完全避开冰山。
6 to one's horror，使某人惊恐的是；below 作副词时可表示“在下面”。

19 What orders were given for evacuation? (Prepare the boats and bring passengers on deck.)
20 What problems with the lifeboats contributed to the loss of life? (Insufficient total capacity, and some boats leaving without a full load.)

Step 3: Composition

In not more than 200 words write an imaginary account of what happened on the Titanic immediately after the order to abandon ship was given. Use the ideas given below. Do not write more than three paragraphs.

On deck, small groups of passengers stood beside the boats, trying to understand what was happening. Some still believed the great ship was the safest place to remain.

An officer called for women and children. Anna lifted her daughter into a lifeboat and followed. The boat began to descend while several seats were still empty. Looking up, she could see people waiting on the brilliantly lit deck. The distance between them grew as the crew rowed away.

For a long time, Anna watched the ship against the dark sky. Then its lights vanished, and cries carried across the water. She held her daughter close and waited in the bitter cold. When another ship finally appeared, she felt relief mixed with grief for those who would never arrive.
